summary: The door's mechanics. New workbench/hand_door.py: one door (DOOR) per process for her hand wherever it drives, Graphite's own window (the desk hand, her_hand_qt) or a program window of yours (K9's a11y_hand). One stop rule: your input while she drives (a press, key or touch the window system delivers to Graphite's window; any X key, button or pointer move not in her ledger, for a program) pauses her at once; her next press is refused (the stop between presses). A paused hand holds the window as it is and waits for your word: Continue (her card's Continue; in her column for a program, Continue authorises the stopped step again and carries her assignment on) or Stop (the window put back as it was). HALT pauses her the same way with its words, and nothing is put back while HALT holds. When she finishes by herself she gives back what was yours (your keyboard and its cursor, the window in front, a menu she left open); what she was asked to show stays. A program window is put back through accessibility (its own allow-list: GrabFocus, SetCaretOffset, SetSelection, AddSelection; menus she opened closed with Escape one level at a time, only while her program has the keyboard; a dialog is never answered or closed by a put back), each part read back: menus, focus, cursor, selection, the control's place on the screen, the window in front. Graphite's window is put back by the planner's moves (what is in front, the selected sheet, what is over the work) and then workbench/hand_door_qt.py (tabs, lists' selection, every scroll, the Field's size and place, your keyboard and its cursor), read back. Changes through her door now go at your dial (0.8.8's hand): hers there, done with its card, trail line and Undo; not hers (Ask first, what always asks, the model's pick alone) staged to wait for your Approve whatever she planned; her card's 'Undo my changes' takes back all of a turn's changes, the latest first (one Undo). Kernel ops hand.door (read), hand.door.continue and hand.door.stop (approve). Shapes and words from D1: '▮▮ stopped by you', '▮▮ stopped by HALT'.

decisions: One door per process for both windows (DOOR in hand_door): the same rule, words and Continue/Stop whichever window she drives.
A touch PAUSES (not ends): the window is held as it is, so 'Continue' can go on and 'Stop' can put it back; D1's '▮▮ stopped by you'.

Her program acts run synchronously in Kernel operations (usually on the window's thread), so the program pause does not block: the op returns 'stopped', the door keeps the pause and the snapshot; a new sequence is refused PAUSED until your word. Your presses that carry her work on (her column's, owner_pressed) count as Continue.

Desk: your touch, hand.stop (its own words: 'the window stays as it is') and Master Stop pause; her card's Stop stops for good and puts the window back (after the press in flight); 'Put my window back' stays for after she finished. Scene P03's expectations hold.
On finish she gives back only what was yours (keyboard and its cursor; for a program also the menus, selection, the window in front), never what she was asked to show; on Stop everything comes back.

Program menus are closed with Escape (XTest, in her ledger) one level at a time, re-read after each, never one more (the probe showed DoAction again does not close a LibreOffice menu and one Escape too many clears your selection); only while her program has the keyboard (else her window is brought forward first). A dialog is never answered or closed by a put back.
Scroll of Graphite's window is put back clamped to the content now; the exchange holding her card is left where it is so her words stay readable.

Changes at the dial: her door no longer refuses changes; a change that is not hers is staged with asked=False (waits whatever the dial says), so a model-picked change never runs; hand.step that is not hers is refused (its own card is your word). Her desk planner still plans navigation only (desk_ops, goals and hand_words untouched): the change path was exercised with a stand-in turn holding one hand.cell act.
Her column: Continue and Stop sit on the hand line's own row (a separate row was squeezed to nothing at 1366x768).

The program window's 'tab' is not kept (AT-SPI page tabs would need a full walk of the window); its 'scroll' is the focused control's place on the screen, compared and scrolled back with Text.ScrollSubstringTo where offered.
